Distribution Data, Geographic Areas, and Species Mapping with sacha

Source: vignettes/spatial-maps.Rmd
spatial-maps.Rmd

Geographic information and first maps

This module combines two kinds of geographic information. locations() returns areas documented by the Catalogue of Life through ChecklistBank. GBIF functions retrieve georeferenced occurrence records. A documented area is not equivalent to a set of observations and does not, by itself, establish current presence at every point within that area.

Start with web queries and the built-in defaults. locations() and locations_md() query the configured ChecklistBank service. gbif_map() creates an interactive map, while gbif_map_md() formats a map for a document.

locations("Bidens andicola")
gbif_map("Bidens andicola")

Use the _md variant in Quarto or R Markdown when you want a figure with a caption and cross-reference identifier:

locations_md("Bidens andicola")
gbif_map_md("Bidens andicola")

GBIF map functions accept source, which defaults to "web"; "local" reads compatible files saved earlier. gbif_save_occurrences() retrieves records from GBIF. The locations() functions do not accept source and do not read GBIF exports. All code chunks in this vignette are displayed but not evaluated during its build.

Saving and reusing occurrences

gbif_save_occurrences() saves occurrence records with query and provenance metadata. A map can also save the records used to create it with save_occurrences = TRUE. Choose one approach for a given retrieval.

gbif_save_occurrences("Bidens andicola")

Or save the records while creating a map:

gbif_map("Bidens andicola", save_occurrences = TRUE)

The default export contains up to 50,000 records. directory sets the base folder; by default, exports are stored under sacha_exports/Family_Genus_species within the working directory. A local map reads those saved files without making a GBIF query:

gbif_map("Bidens andicola", source = "local")

Local calls require an export for the same taxon in the selected directory. They do not download missing records. For repeatable document output, use the _md function and set results='asis' on its R Markdown chunk.

Interactive and static maps

gbif_map() defaults to an interactive Leaflet map. Use mode = "static" to return a ggplot2 map. export_image = TRUE writes a PNG as well; it does not change the map object returned by the function.

gbif_map("Bidens andicola", mode = "static", export_image = TRUE)

For a document, gbif_map_md() selects a mode from the output format unless mode is supplied. Static figures can be sized with fig_width and fig_height; colour, dpi, and static_legend_position adjust the saved map’s appearance when needed.

gbif_map_md("Bidens andicola", mode = "static")

The limit argument controls the maximum number of occurrences used by a map. When species is supplied, the package resolves an exact species-level match; taxon_id accepts a COL XR key instead. date filters datasets by the GBIF registry creation date (createdDate), not by the occurrence date.

Cropped maps

gbif_map_crop() and gbif_map_crop_md() add a study area using crop_area, crop_box, or crop_vector. crop_area accepts a country name or code. crop_box uses WGS 84 decimal degrees in the order xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax; an optional fifth value labels the area. crop_vector accepts a KML or ESRI Shapefile path. Use only one of crop_area and crop_vector; crop_box can be combined with either one.

The default distribution = "local" shows records inside the crop. distribution = "global" shows available species records in the map frame and uses the selected area as a reference boundary. With a web source and a local distribution, the selected country or geometry is sent to GBIF as a spatial filter.

gbif_map_crop("Bidens andicola", crop_area = "Ecuador")

The same crop can be rendered in a document. This example adds a rectangular boundary around continental Ecuador:

gbif_map_crop_md(
  "Bidens andicola",
  crop_box = c(-82.5, -5.5, -75.0, 1.6, "Ecuador continental"),
  distribution = "global",
  mode = "static"
)

A KML or Shapefile can be used when a study boundary is already available. KML reading requires a GDAL installation with its KML driver.

gbif_map_crop("Bidens andicola", crop_vector = "study_boundary.kml")

Save and map a cropped export locally

To reuse a particular crop, save it with the same area definition and then select that crop when mapping. The saved export includes its boundary and metadata.

gbif_save_occurrences("Bidens andicola", crop_area = "Ecuador")

gbif_map_crop(
  "Bidens andicola",
  crop_area = "Ecuador",
  source = "local",
  local_export = "crop"
)

Alternatively, save a full-species export with gbif_save_occurrences("Bidens andicola"), then use source = "local" with local_export = "species" to apply a crop to those records. Local exports that cover only a crop represent only their saved geographic coverage; they do not establish worldwide coverage.

Provenance and GBIF download DOI

For an ordinary retrieval, gbif_save_occurrences() uses the occurrence search service. Set generate_doi = TRUE to request a registered GBIF download and save its DOI in the metadata. This requires GBIF_USER, GBIF_PWD, and GBIF_EMAIL to be available in the R session. Keep credentials outside the vignette and package source.

gbif_save_occurrences("Bidens andicola", generate_doi = TRUE)

The default limit is 50,000 records; limit = NULL requests all available matching records and is only valid with generate_doi = TRUE. The optional date argument filters by the registry’s createdDate, not by observation date. taxon_id can be supplied instead of the species name when a COL XR key is available. Review the saved metadata and cite the DOI assigned to that specific download in any publication.

Figures in Quarto and R Markdown

For chunks that call _md map functions, use results='asis' so the renderer processes the figure markup. Static document figures accept fig_width and fig_height; interactive widgets use their container sizing. Figure identifiers include the species and, for cropped maps, the normalized area label. Check the identifier in the rendered document before using it in a cross-reference.

For guidance on querying and attributing records, see the GBIF API documentation.
